newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel eases closure of West Bank and Gaza.
newsitem.headline: Israel eases closure of West Bank and Gaza.

text.p: The Israeli army said on Monday it would permit more Palestinians to work in Israel, easing a closure imposed on the West Bank and Gaza last month after an Islamist bombing of a Tel Aviv cafe.

"The minister of defence and chief of staff decided that as of Tuesday morning workers from the West Bank and Gaza Strip who are married and over the age of 30 will be allowed to come and work in Israel, a military statement said.
"It was also decided to renew (family) visits to (Palestinian) security prisoners on a scale of 300 visitors per day," it added.

It was not immediately clear how many Palestinians would benefit from the lowering of the minimum age for a work permit from 35 to 30. Israel believes the marriage requirement and age limit cut the risk of suicide bombers entering its territory.
The army announced the move on the eve of a Europe-Mediterranean conference in Malta which Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy will attend.

The European Union has been trying to arrange a meeting between the two in an effort to end an Israeli-Palestinian crisis touched off by Israel's groundbreaking on March 18 for a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said on Monday that U.S. envoy Dennis Ross would go to the Middle East this week for talks with Israeli and Palestinian leaders on reviving the stalled peace process.

Palestinian officials said about 10,000 Palestinian workers entered the Jewish state on Sunday when Israel first eased the closure it clamped on the West Bank and Gaza after the March 21 blast which killed the bomber and three Israeli women.
Israel has periodically sealed off the West Bank and Gaza for security reasons since parts of the territories fell under Palestinian self-rule in 1994 under a Israeli-PLO peace deal.
More than 60,000 Palestinians held jobs in Israel before 1994.
